cards.title: Introduction to Vue Router
cards.content:
Vue Router is the official router for Vue.js. It deeply integrates with Vue.js core to make building Single Page Applications (SPAs) with Vue a breeze.

Key features include:

  • Nested route/view mapping
  • Modular, component-based router configuration
  • Route params, query, wildcards
  • View transitions powered by Vue's transition system
  • Fine-grained navigation control

cards.title: Setting Up Vue Router
cards.content:
To install Vue Router in a Vue 3 project, use npm:

npm install vue-router@4

Then define your routes and create the router instance:

import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router'
import Home from './views/Home.vue'
import About from './views/About.vue'

const routes = [
  { path: '/', component: Home },
  { path: '/about', component: About }
]

const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHistory(),
  routes
})

export default router

cards.title: Router History Mode
cards.content: To use HTML5 History mode in Vue Router, we use the function called ____createWebHistory____.

cards.title: Rendering Routes with RouterView
cards.content:
Once the router is installed and registered in your main app, you need to use the <RouterView> component to display the matched component for the current route.

<template>
  <div id="app">
    <nav>
      <router-link to="/">Home</router-link> |
      <router-link to="/about">About</router-link>
    </nav>
    <router-view></router-view>
  </div>
</template>

cards.title: Dynamic Route Matching with Params
cards.content:
Often you need to map routes with the given pattern to the same component. For example, a User component should be rendered for all users, but with different user IDs.

const routes = [
  // dynamic segments start with a colon
  { path: '/user/:id', component: User }
]

Inside the component, you can access the route parameter using useRoute().params.id.

steps: Define route objects with path and component properties
Create the router instance using createRouter and createWebHistory
Register the router with the Vue application instance using .use(router)
Add <router-view> and <router-link> in your root component

cards.title: Nested Routes
cards.content:
Real application UIs are usually composed of multiple levels of nested components. Vue Router allows you to express this relationship using the children option.

const routes = [
  {
    path: '/user/:id',
    component: User,
    children: [
      {
        // UserProfile will be rendered inside User's 
        // when /user/:id/profile is matched
        path: 'profile',
        component: UserProfile,
      },
      {
        // UserPosts will be rendered inside User's 
        // when /user/:id/posts is matched
        path: 'posts',
        component: UserPosts,
      },
    ],
  },
]

cards.title: Navigation Guards
cards.content:
Navigation guards provided by Vue Router are primarily used to guard navigations either by redirecting it or canceling it. There are global guards, per-route guards, and in-component guards.

router.beforeEach((to, from) => {
  // instead of needless checking we use a helper function to check auth
  if (!isAuthenticated && to.name !== 'Login') {
    // redirect the user to the login page
    return { name: 'Login' }
  }
})
